3. The petitioners' case is that they had their ancestral home on 2.65 acres out of a total of 5.80 acres of Khatian No. 1358 of mouzaMoulvi Bazar Town which comprises several houses, tank, graveyard, gardens etc. wherein the petitioners have been living for generations now. The respondent No.4 Syed Mohsin Ali, his six brothers, two sisters and mother mutated their names in respect of the entire land of 5.80 acres of the above khatian No. 1358 on the basis of a registered Kabala No. 5879 executed and registered on 31.10.55 by one Keramat Ali in favour of Syed Ashraf Ali, deceased father of the said respondent No.4. The said Keramat Ali auction purchased the entire land of 5.80 acres of the said khatian No. 1358 on 25.9.54 for arrears of rent. The auction purchaser Keramat Ali however sold only 3.15 acres of the khatian land out of 5.80 acres to late Syed Ashraf Ali, father of the respondent No.4. The balance 2.65 acres of ancestral homestead continued to remain in the possession of the petitioners and their predecessors. The predecessors of the petitioners obtained a registered Muktipatra dated 8.5.79 from one of the sons of auction purchaser Keramat Ali, namely HabiburRahman. Thereafter the predecessors of the petitioners by executing and registering three separate deeds of gift, all dated 5.11.78, transferred their right, title and interest in the case land to the petitioners and delivered physical possession thereof to them. The petitioners thereafter instituted Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979 be- fore the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvibazar. After compliance of necessary formalities all the three mutation cases were allowed vide order dated 13.11.79. The respondent No.4 Syed Mohsin Ali and his 5 brothers filed an objection petition before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1979 was started. The par- ties were notified. After hearing the parties the Circle Officer forwarded the case record to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet for necessary action with a detailed report as he found the case to be complicated. Then the respondent No.4 preferred an appeal before the Additional Deputy Com- missioner (Revenue), Sylhet under section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, shortly the Act, against the Order dated 13.11.79 passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar whereupon Mutation Appeal Case No. 24 of 1979- 80 was started and the petitioners were notified. By his order dated 10.9.80 the Additional Deputy Com- missioner, Sylhet after hearing the parties rejected the appeal of the respondent No.4 and upheld the or- der dated 13.1l.79 passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvibazar in Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979. Against the aforesaid order of the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet the respondent No.4 preferred an appeal before the Com- missioner, Chittagong Division being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 223 of 1980 under section 147 of the Act which was heard and disposed of by the Additional Commissioner, Chittagong Division by his order dated 15.12.82 dismissing the same and con-firming the order dated 10.9.80 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet. 

 4. In the meanwhile the Board of Land Administration Act, 1980 (Act No. XIII of 1981), shortly the Board Act, came into force on 30th June, 1981 whereby a Board of Land Administration was constituted with the authority to dispose of all statutory appeals vide memo No. lOM-13/82/1224-Estt. dated 3.9.82 (Annexure I). The respondent No.4 being aggrieved by the order dated 15.12.82 passed by the Additional Commissioner Chittagong Division preferred an appeal before the Board of Land Administration. The appeal was admitted, reports were called for from the Additional Commissioner, Chittagong Division and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet. Upon perusal of the reports and hearing the parties the Board of Land Administration in Appeal Case No. 43 of 1983 by order dated 1l.l.84 contained in memo No. VI-43/ 83/92-Appeal dated 24.l.84 (Annexure K) rejected the appeal. Under section 4 of the Board Act a right of review within 60 days of the order has been provided for but the respondent No. 4 did not prefer any application for review. Instead, he preferred an incompetent appeal before the Ministry of Land Ad- ministration and Land Reforms which was admitted by the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms, respondent No.1, on 13.1l.84 and records were called for. No notice however was served on the petitioners. In the light of orders of the Board of Land Administration (Annexure K) the petitioners went to Tahsil Office, Moulvi Bazar for payment of rent for 1392 B.S. in the last week of May, 1985 when to their surprise they came to know that the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms has since reversed the order of the Board of Land Administration exercising appellate powers under section 147 of the Act in a mutation proceeding under section 143 of the Act, allowing the objection of the respondent No.4. The petitioner No.1 came to know definitely about the aforesaid order on 2.6.85 when he came to Dhaka. A true copy of the said order was annexed as Annexure M which is the first impugned order. 

 8. It is stated therein that the aforesaid 5.80 acres of land of the aforesaid khatian originally be-longed to Syed Ashraf Ali, the father of respondent No.4, and Syed Ashraf Ali gifted the same to his wife SyedaAktarunnessaKhanam in lieu of her dower. The said property was sold in auction for arrears of rent and was purchased by Keramat Ali when Syed Ashraf Ali and his wife were living in Calcutta. Coming to know of the auction sale Syed Ashraf Ali obtained a kabala in his own name for valuable consideration from the said auction purchaser Keramat Ali in respect of the whole of the auction sold property, namely 5.80 acres, by kabala No. 5879 dated 31.10.55. But unfortunately the deed writer through bonafide mistake wrote 3.15 acres in place of the whole of the auction sold property, namely 5.80 acres. The recipient of the said kabala, Syed Ashraf Ali, was not aware of the said mistake in the deed as he remained in possession of the whole of 5.80 acres all along, including the period from the date of auction upto the date of the aforesaid kabala. 

 9. During the rent roll operations in 1958 the entire 5.80 acres of land was wrongly recorded in the names of Syed Ashraf Ali and his brother Syed Ankar Ali, the latter having no title to or interest in the aforesaid property. In 1964 Syed Ashraf Ali allowed his nephews, namely, Syed Abdul Mannan, Syed Mozammel Ali and Syed SalehMasud to live in a portion of the aforesaid property having structures thereon, as his licencees. In 1965 Syed Ashraf Ali corrected the khatian by filing Case No. 331 of 1965 before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar by striking out of the name of his brother Syed Ankar Ali from the khatian. It is therefore absolutely incorrect that the balance 2.65 acres of ancestral home- stead continued to remain in possessive of the petitioners and their predecessors. Three nephews of Syed Ashraf Ali were only in possession of a part of the property in question. Syed Ashraf Ali died in 1970. Thereafter the heirs of Syed Ashraf Ali, namely, the respondent No.4 and his brothers and sisters requested the said licencees to surrender possession of the structures to them. At this stage they became hostile and instead of complying with the request they approached one of the sons of auction purchaser Keramat Ali, namely HabiburRahman, and obtained a so-called Muktipatrafrom him in respect of 2.65 acres out of the khatian taking advantage of mistake in respect of area in Syed Ashraf Ali's kahala dated 31.10.55 The said Muktipatra dated 8.5.79 was obtained in the names of the three licencees of Syed Ashraf Ali and another, namely Syed Abdun Noor. The Muktipatra is collusive and fraudulent. Later, Syed Abdun Noor purported to gift .64 acres of land in favour of his brother's son, namely petitioner No. 1, on 26.10.79. Syed Abdul Mannan purported to gift .65 acre on the same day to his wife who is the petitioner No. 2. Syed SalehMasud purported to gift .65 acres of land on the same day to his wife, petitioner No.3. The said donors being mere licencees and having no title to the land in question, the petitioners got no title to or interest in the lands purported to have been gifted to them. It has also been stated that after completing the aforesaid collusive and fraudulent transactions the petitioners applied to the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar for mutation of their names whereupon their names were mutated in respect of 1.95 acres by an ex parte order dated 13.11.79. No notice of the aforesaid mutation ease was either issued or served upon the respondent No.4 and the order of mutation was passed in spite of objection raised by the Tahsildar which will appear from the records of the Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979. Thereafter the respondent No.4 has more or less accepted the petitioners' description of the progress of the case from the stage of the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar upto the Board of Land Administration. The said respondent however justifies his appeal before the Ministry of Land Administration on the ground that the law does not oust the Government's authority to decide a matter in respect of which the Board of Land Administration exercises appellate power. 

 18. Me. Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 in WritPetition No. 425 of 1985, faced with this difficulty, feebly argued that in spite of the statutory amendment relegating to the Board of Land Administrationthe powers of hearing and disposal of appeals and revisions, the Government, as the overall supervisory authority of all revenue officers and revenue administration, possesses the inherent jurisdiction to revise and modify any order passed by the Board of LandAdministration. Therefore, even if the appeal of the respondent NO.4 to the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms was incompetent, it can be treated as a provisional application and the Government should be deemed to have exercised its inherent provisional power in disposing of the same.

 24. The question is, is such mutation permit- ted under section 143 of the Act? Chapter IV of the Act contains an elaborate procedure for preparing the record-of-rights and also for hearing objections from parties concerned. S.A. khatian No. 1358 was pre- pared in the joint names of Syed Ashraf Ali and his brother Syed Ankar Ali during the rent roll operations in 1958. No objections were filed by the predecessors of the respondent Nos. 4-6. Thekhatian was corrected in 1965 by Syed Ashraf Ali and thereafter it stood in his sole name. After his death in 1970, his heirs and successors mutated their names in Mutation Case No. 75 of 1973-74. No objections were filed at that time. 

 30. It is well-established that a determination that is erroneous in law can be set aside if the error goes to jurisdiction or if the error is apparent on the face of the record. We find that the Board of Land Ad- ministration has misdirected itself as to the question of law involved in this case and has decided matters which are not within its jurisdiction to decide under scction143. We arc of the opinion that under such circumstances the decision of the Board of Land Administration is liable to interference by this Court.

 32. In the unreported decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh and others-Vs- MariumKhatun and others (Civil Appeal No.8 of 1972) the facts are that the respondent who, along with others took settlement of land from Zaminders and were in in possession thereof, challenged the or- der of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faridpur cancelling the names of the respondent and his co-sharers from the record of rights which were recorded in the name of the then Province of East Pakistan. By four different orders from 1960 to 1963 the Revenue Settlement Officer corrected the record of rights and inserted the names of the respondent and his co-sharers in the disputed khatian. The Deputy Commissioner of Faridpur purchased some of the land in dispute from the respondent in 1964, but on 17.10.66 the respondent and his co-sharers were served with notice to show cause why the record of rights shall not be changed in favour of the Province of East Pakistan. The respondent showed cause but the Additional Deputy Com- missioner (Revenue), Faridpur cancelled the names of the respondent and his co-sharers by order dated 13.7.67 and inserted the name of the Province of East Pakistan in respect of the disputed Khatian. The case of the Province of East Pakistan was that the names of the respondent and his co-sharers were re- corded as a result of fraudulent transaction between the respondent and his co-sharers on the one hand and some of the revenue authorities on the other.
